---
title: "Dropping columns"
---

Dropping columns removes model variables that might lead to underidentified models, or models that take a long time to fit.
shoez has three filter steps for it: one for correlated columns and two for
columns with little or no variance.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Key points"}
* Correlated variables - model may not fit otherwise
* Near zero variance
* Filters are not a stage of the [eight-step order](four-stages-eight-steps.qmd);
  they run after stage 1 and again after the dummy step.
:::

## Setup

```{python}
from shoez import Recipe, StepDropCorr, StepDropNearZeroVariance, StepDropZeroVariance
from shoez import Selectors as s
from shoez.data import ames_mini, beans
```

## Drop one of each highly correlated pair

`StepDropCorr(columns, threshold=...)` drops one column from each pair whose
correlation exceeds the threshold, keeping the other. In the Ames subset,
`Garage_Cars` and `Garage_Area` say nearly the same thing (correlation 0.89),
so one of them goes:

```{python}
recipe = Recipe(data=ames_mini, target="Sale_Price").add(
    StepDropCorr(s.numeric_features(), threshold=0.8)
)
fitted = recipe.fit(ames_mini)
fitted.transform(ames_mini).columns
```

The default threshold is 0.9. The dry beans data shows how much a
correlated set can collapse: its 16 shape measurements lose 9 of their
number.

```{python}
recipe = Recipe(data=beans, target="class").add(StepDropCorr(s.numeric_features()))
fitted = recipe.fit(beans)
fitted.transform(beans).columns
```

## Drop columns with little or no variance

`StepDropNearZeroVariance(columns)` drops columns that are nearly constant,
which a model can only overfit to. `Street` is the case here: 12 of 2,930
houses are on a gravel road.

```{python}
recipe = Recipe(data=ames_mini, target="Sale_Price").add(
    StepDropNearZeroVariance(s.features())
)
fitted = recipe.fit(ames_mini)
fitted.transform(ames_mini).columns
```

`StepDropZeroVariance` is the strict version: it drops only columns that are
completely constant or all missing. Its usual place is right after a dummy
step, where a level that is present in the schema but absent from the
training rows becomes an all-zero indicator column.

## Missing values are a row problem

Filters remove columns. Rows with missing values are a different problem,
handled by imputation rather than removal, and they are covered on
[Ensure robust to new data](ensure-robust-to-new-data.qmd).
